attrs.text:
read @utils/test_normalizer.sh.
It currently takes two params a jsonl file and the name where normalized output must be written.
Your job is add following functionality using shell script only.
  1. add -h --help.
  2. Add a functionality so a whole folder full of jsonl files can be processed. For examle look at @../../../traces/Users/. Only process the jsonl files. You will recurse thru all the subfolders. Users will provide a target dir -p <path_name>. The path_name must exist. The corresponding folder structure must follow the exact folder structure that is present in the source including names. That is important.
 3. A different run may point to the same path_name but subfolders and files in the source could be different. 
 4. If a particular file or folder exist the default behavior is not to overwrite. Unless -f/--force is specified.
 5. At the end of rung it must produce a small run_results.json (default) that writes results of every file processed, errors, duplicate found, overwritten etc. -r/--result <filename> can override the results json file. 

I asking you to stick to shell script since the python code wrapped by shell script processes a single file today. We may imporove that later but want to avoid modifying the py file.
Have you ran against the target I pointed out as an example.
